calibration_notes: Cosmetic credit-score '$' corruptions (platinum_001 '$750', business_platinum_001 '$765', silver_001 '$680') and the business_platinum_001 title are rated as Minor issues in 043, 044, 045, 047 (making each task Minor) and 048. Under calibration.md these are notes because no gold value depends on them, so 043/044/045/047 should be None. By contrast, 029's EcoCard '$5.00 points' is correctly Minor because it is the deciding rate for a disputed transaction.

Missing required documents are rated inconsistently. 029 (doc_007 omitted) is rated Minor, but 050 (no tier mapping in required_documents) is left in notes, and 037/038 (doc_016, the only source of the dispute-history tool needed for provisional-credit criterion 4) are not mentioned. Calibration says Minor for all of them.

Unscripted resolution_requested gets three severities: 039 Minor, 040 Major (Comcast), 041 Blocker (XFINITY). By the letter of the calibration ('Major when there is no default'), 039's issue is Major-class, since doc_014 only says 'Ask user what resolution they want'. The scenario's '$50 extra' entails the gold, which makes Minor defensible but unstated. 041's Blocker is justified by the precise amount 69.99 resting on 'around $120'. 039 and 040 are Major anyway, so no task severity changes.

040's fixture date inconsistency (dispute noticed and submitted before its purchase date) is rated a Minor issue even though no count or gold value depends on it. By analogy with the cosmetic-defect rule it should be a note.

Closure-reason ambiguity under exact closure_reason grading (045 found_better_card vs not_using_card/simplifying_finances, 047 annual_fee vs not_using_card, 048 unhappy_with_rewards vs not_using_card, 049 annual_fee vs unhappy_with_rewards) is consistently treated as residual risk in notes. I agree in each case, because the customer's first or explicit reason maps to the gold.
The ACTION-leniency class (032/033/034) and the unscripted-expedited class (038/039/054) are applied consistently as Minor.
methodology_note: The review's grading model matches the snapshot code, and its replay-based claims reproduced in every case I re-ran (about 40 variant replays across 15 tasks, using a harness that builds the environment with the gold-derived read allowlist). The substantive Blocker and Major calls (029, 039, 040, 041, 046, 048, 049, 053) hold. The main method weakness is calibration rather than evidence. Cosmetic doc corruptions were turned into task-level Minor ratings, and the missing-required-document rule was applied only when the gap was dramatic. Two blind spots are worth a pass across the rest of the benchmark. First, some fixtures disagree with derived data: 046's dispute last-4 7823 matches neither of the user's cards and its transaction does not exist, and 054's account-field last-4 7823 contradicts the tool-derived 0791. Second, a provisional-credit decision depends on doc_016 in tasks that omit it from required_documents.
